title: A Thorn for the Wolf
premise: Ivo Nystrom can hear what beasts think, a gift punishable by burning, and he has spent his life hiding it behind guild ledgers and careful silence. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, the country of Vessany begins to unwrite itself, and Ivo discovers the guild's impossible trade is powered by the same magic eating the land. Hunted by the wolf-pack that guards the last true door and bound to a disgraced ward-keeper who knows his secret, Ivo must choose between exposing his gift to save the found family he's built or letting Vessany die quietly. In the end he speaks with the wolves' own voice to reopen the door, sacrificing the guild's hoarded magic and his anonymity, and walks out of a dying country into an exile that finally feels like belonging.
about_author: Wren Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who keep dangerous secrets in ordinary places, and live somewhere cold with too many dogs.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the eve of the winter audit, Ivo balances the guild's ledgers while concealing the whispers of rats and ravens in the walls. The border wards shatter, the stars extinguish, and guildmaster Odile reveals the vault holds something alive. The beat is dread: the ordinary world cracks open, and Ivo's silence becomes complicity.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Remember
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with interludes from ward-keeper Sefa. Fleeing the unraveling capital, Ivo and Sefa are captured by the wolf-pack guarding the last door out of Vessany. Ivo's gift slips free when he answers a wolf aloud, and Sefa covers for him. The beat is reluctant trust: two liars and a pack decide, provisionally, not to kill each other.

chapters.title: A Country Unwriting Itself
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ivo and the alpha wolf, Grey-Marrow. The party crosses villages being erased from memory itself; Odile's hunters close in, demanding the vault-beast as payment to save the guild alone. Ivo learns the door requires a voice the land trusts. The beat is betrayal and choice: loyalty to the guild wars against the truth he owes his new pack.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the door, Ivo speaks openly in every beast-tongue at once, offering the guild's hoarded magic back to the land so Vessany can end honestly instead of screaming. Grey-Marrow holds the threshold; Sefa chooses exile over duty. The beat is bittersweet resolution: the door opens, the family walks through, and Ivo stops hiding his voice.
